title: Beyond Language Processing: LLMs Rules-Injected Instruction Tuning for Traffic Prediction

problem.claim: Accurate traffic prediction requires modeling heterogeneous traffic data.

gap.claim: LLM pre-training provides primarily qualitative and broad knowledge rather than the fine-grained, context-specific quantitative dependencies required for accurate traffic prediction, which can reduce instruction-tuning effectiveness.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs offer contextual integration and multi-step reasoning capabilities with potential for modeling heterogeneous traffic data.
Broad qualitative pre-training knowledge does not supply the quantitative dependencies needed for accurate traffic prediction.
The mismatch between pre-training knowledge and task requirements can reduce the effectiveness of instruction tuning for downstream tasks.

source_observation.claim: Broad pre-training knowledge may not provide the fine-grained quantitative dependencies required by a specialized prediction task.

interpretation.claim: Adapting a general-purpose model may require task-specific quantitative structure in addition to general contextual knowledge.

application.claim: When applying LLMs to quantitative forecasting, assess whether the adaptation method supplies context-specific dependencies needed by the task.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this mismatch affects every traffic-prediction setting or adaptation method.

unknowns: The abstract units do not specify the proposed method or rules-injection mechanism.
No datasets, baselines, metrics, quantitative results, or experimental conditions are provided.
